Table 1 from the document "Sustainable Direct Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Solvent Recovery of Electrode Materials" shows the Hansen solubility parameters of PVDF, NMP, DMF, and EG.

| Compound | δd [MPa]^1/2 | δp [MPa]^1/2 | δh [MPa]^1/2 | Ra [MPa]^1/2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PVDF | 17.2 | 12.5 | 9.2 | – |
| NMP | 18.4 | 12.3 | 7.2 | 2.3 |
| DMF | 17.4 | 13.7 | 11.3 | 2.4 |
| EG | 17.0 | 11.0 | 26.0 | 16.9 |

The solvent with the strongest hydrogen bonding is EG, with a δh value of 26.0 MPa^1/2. This is because EG has two hydroxyl groups in one molecule, which can form strong hydrogen bonds with the aluminum surface.

EG is not used for delamination because it causes corrosion of the aluminum foil due to lithium leaching from the NMC cathode, making the water solution basic. This leads to the formation of Al(OH)3 precipitates on the cathode surfaces, contaminating the NMC particles.
